bull.b: Positive Phase 2a results provide clinical validation for NEO100 in recurrent high-grade glioma, an area with limited treatment options. If confirmed in subsequent development, the observed disease control and survival could support regulatory progress, differentiation, and a durable commercial opportunity.

Patent protection through 2038 can help preserve exclusivity around NeOnc’s CNS drug candidates and delivery technologies. Combined with multiple NEO100 and NEO212 development programs, this platform may support sustained competitive differentiation if clinical and regulatory milestones are achieved.

International IND clearances expand the settings in which NeOnc can develop its candidates and run studies, complementing U.S. work. A broader trial footprint may improve development flexibility, increase access to patients, and create more opportunities to advance the pipeline toward registration.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated commercial revenue scale, while operating costs substantially exceed reported sales. Extremely large losses relative to revenue indicate that commercialization remains distant or uncertain and that future progress depends heavily on successful clinical execution and additional funding.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means NeOnc is consuming capital to fund its operations and clinical programs rather than generating internal financing. The deterioration from 2024 increases the likelihood of recurring fundraising and could constrain the pace or breadth of future development.

Deeply negative equity weakens financial flexibility and signals that accumulated losses have overwhelmed the company’s capital base. Although the recent financing adds liquidity, issuing shares and warrants can dilute existing holders, while continued losses may require further capital and preserve balance-sheet pressure.
